examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Quicksort's costs depend on pivot choice, partition scheme and equal-key handling. Repeated extreme pivots create quadratic comparisons and linear recursion depth. Randomized pivots give expected n log n work, without removing the worst case. Partitioning can be in place while recursion still needs stack space. Recursing on the smaller part and iterating on the larger can bound stack depth independently of pivot balance.

**Key relationship:** Worst split: T(n)=T(n−1)+Θ(n)=Θ(n²)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Specify pivot and partition conventions.
2. Record partition sizes.
3. Separate expected work, worst work and auxiliary stack.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: State pivot-selection and partition conventions. Balanced partitions give logarithmic depth; consistently extreme pivots give linear depth and quadratic work. Expected O(n log n) needs randomization or a distribution assumption. Equal keys can defeat two-way partitioning unless handled carefully.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Six distinct keys arrive sorted. Quicksort always chooses the last pivot and compares it with every other key in its partition. How many pivot comparisons occur?

**Answer: 15.** Every pivot is the maximum. Comparisons are 5+4+3+2+1=15, the n(n−1)/2 worst case for this convention.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
In-place partitioning does not eliminate recursive stack space. Recurse on the smaller side and iterate over the larger side to bound stack depth.

Randomized quicksort has a good expected bound, not a deterministic worst-case logarithmic-depth guarantee.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Sorted distinct input with always-largest pivot gives runtime:

- **A.** Θ(n²)
- **B.** Θ(log n)
- **C.** Θ(n)
- **D.** Θ(n log n)

**Answer: A.** Partitions have sizes n−1 and 0 repeatedly, summing (n−1)+(n−2)+…+1 comparisons.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Randomization can give expected O(n log n)
- **B.** Quicksort has no quadratic input
- **C.** Two-way partitions may handle equal keys poorly
- **D.** In-place partitioning alone does not eliminate call-stack memory

**Answer: A, C, D.** Expected bounds do not remove all bad pivot outcomes, so B is false.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Seven sorted distinct keys use last-element pivots, comparing each other key once per partition. Comparisons?



**Answer: 21.** Worst-case comparisons=6+5+4+3+2+1=21.
